name: Budget Manager
description: Enforces hard spending limits on remote API usage. Tracks actual spend per request (reported by Remote API Client after each call). Maintains running totals for configurable periods: daily, weekly, monthly. Persists budget state to disk (JSON) via atomic writes for crash-safe survival across restarts. Uses a write-ahead reservation pattern: authorize() reserves estimated cost before API call, record_spend() reconciles with actual cost afterward. A crash between authorize and record conservatively counts the estimate. Phase-agnostic: returns allowed/denied decisions; the orchestrator decides whether denial means raising BudgetExhaustedError (Phase 1) or switching to local-only mode with warning (Phase 2/3). All monetary values use Decimal (stdlib) to avoid floating-point drift over thousands of micro-transactions. Period boundary rollovers are checked on every authorize() call using zoneinfo-aware timestamps. Single-threaded concurrency model: check-then-spend is atomic with no race conditions. Reporting (savings, cost trajectory) is provided as read-only query methods separated from the enforce/record write path.

functions.name: __init__
functions.description: Constructs a BudgetManager instance. Loads existing state from disk if state file exists, otherwise initializes fresh state. Validates config strictly — fails fast on invalid config. If state file exists but fails validation, raises BudgetStateCorruptedError. functions.name: authorize
functions.description: Checks whether a remote API request with the given estimated cost is allowed under ALL active period budgets. If allowed, reserves the estimated_cost in all active periods (write-ahead pattern) and persists state. If denied, returns rich denial context. The caller (orchestrator) decides behavior based on allowed/denied and current phase. On every call, checks for period boundary crossover and performs rollover if needed (archives completed period, resets running totals). This is the primary enforcement point — called before every remote API request.

inputs.description: Estimated cost of the pending remote API request. Must be positive. The reservation amount if authorized.

validators.error_message: estimated_cost must be a positive Decimal.

functions.name: record_spend
functions.description: Records the actual spend for a completed remote API request. Reconciles the reservation made by authorize(): removes the estimated reservation and adds the actual confirmed spend. Called by Remote API Client after each successful API call. Persists state atomically after recording. If actual cost differs from estimated, the difference adjusts the period totals accordingly.

inputs.description: Actual cost reported by the remote API after request completion. Must be non-negative.

validators.error_message: actual_cost must be a non-negative Decimal.

inputs.name: estimated_cost
inputs.description: The estimated cost that was originally reserved by authorize(). Used to release the reservation. Must match the value passed to authorize().

validators.error_message: estimated_cost must be a positive Decimal.

inputs.name: metadata
inputs.description: Metadata for auditing: request_id, model, tokens, task type, timestamp.

invariants: All monetary values (spend, limits, savings, costs) are represented as Decimal — never float.

confirmed_spend + reserved_spend <= limit is enforced by authorize() for all active periods when authorization is granted. The effective spend (confirmed + reserved) never exceeds the limit at the moment of authorization.
reserved_spend is always non-negative (clamped to zero floor on release/reconciliation).
confirmed_spend is always non-negative and monotonically increasing within a period.
In-memory BudgetState is always authoritative over the disk-persisted state. Disk is for crash recovery only.
State file writes are atomic: write to temp file, fsync, rename. No partial writes are possible.
Period boundary rollover is checked on every authorize() and remaining_budget() call. Stale periods are always archived before evaluation.
historical_periods list length never exceeds config.max_historical_periods. Oldest entries are evicted first.
The budget manager is phase-agnostic: it returns BudgetAuthorizationResult and never raises BudgetExhaustedError. Phase-specific behavior is the orchestrator's responsibility.
Single-threaded execution model: authorize-then-spend is atomic with no race conditions. No concurrent calls to authorize() or record_spend() are supported.
Every state mutation (authorize, record_spend, release_reservation, record_local_request, reset_state) triggers an atomic persist. Persistence failure does not roll back the in-memory mutation.
All timestamps are timezone-aware using zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(config.timezone). No naive datetimes.
No global state: all state flows through the BudgetManager instance and its injected BudgetConfig.
